title: Unexpected usage spike from retry + KV cache replay affecting Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported unexpectedly high token usage and billing charges over a 24-72 hour window. Initial signals show correlated spikes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Preliminary investigation suggests an interaction between request retry logic and prefix/KV cache replay that produced duplicate accounting for generated tokens in the billing pipeline. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, root cause analysis, and rollout of a fix across all deployment modes.
impact_summary: Three customers (one large fintech, one e-commerce, one healthcare pilot) saw 3x–8x token usage spikes on day X. Billing dashboards showed inflated daily totals, leading to billing disputes and an enterprise escalation. Estimated revenue/regressions exposure: medium-high; operational load high due to support and SRE involvement.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit a streaming generation request with partial response ACK and client-side retry after network blip
2) Server-side serving runtime resumes generation using KV cache replay path to continue the token stream
3) Retry path replays the same prefix but a race causes accounting middleware to increment token counters twice
4) In load tests, enabling aggressive batching + KV cache hit ratio increases the likelihood of double-counting
5) Reproduction reliably observed in Dedicated and Hosted; Private reproduction requires exact KV cache config and was reproduced in customer staging environment
initial_triage: SRE and billing engineering confirmed that accounting events were emitted twice for the same logical generation. Event sequencing in the metering pipeline did not dedupe in the presence of identical session IDs when replayed within a short window. A temporary mitigation to stop billing variance was identified and applied to Hosted within 6 hours (rate-limited accounting ingest).
mitigation: Applied rate-limit throttle on accounting ingest for hosted (rolled 2025-02-15 03:00 UTC)
Opened emergency feature flag to disable KV cache replay accounting in Dedicated control plane (flag: disable-replay-accounting)
Guided three affected customers with manual crediting and customer-facing incident notes, offered immediate refunds where applicable
Added dashboard alert for >2x hourly variance vs 7-day median for affected accounts
root_cause: Race condition between the retry coordinator and the accounting middleware: when a client retry triggers a server-side replay using the KV cache, the serving runtime emitted two 'tokens_generated' events with identical session_id but different request_id. The metering pipeline's event dedup key used request_id, not session_id + sequence_range, so duplicates were counted. In addition, an optimizer added sub-second batching to improve throughput which coalesced replayed segments into single accounting increments, masking the issue in unit tests but amplifying it in production.
fix_plan: Primary fix: change metering dedup key to canonicalize on (customer_id, session_id, token_range_start, token_range_end) and add a short-lived replay window (30s) where duplicates are ignored
Runtime change: tag replayed KV-cache segments with replay=true and include replay_nonce to help dedup logic
Telemetry: emit accounting debug logs when accounting events for the same session_id appear within 60s
Rollout strategy: staged rollout to Hosted (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%), then Dedicated customers by contacting account owners, and provide a hotfix package for Private customers to apply
Backfill: run a reconciliation job to identify and reverse double-counted events over the incident window for customers who were impacted
verification_plan: Automated tests: add integration test with simulated retry + KV replay to assert single accounting event per token_range
Canary verification: monitor billing ingest rate and per-customer hourly variance during canary windows
Customer validation: coordinate with impacted customers to confirm corrected usage after backfill
Postmortem metrics: reduce frequency of >2x variance alerts to baseline within 48 hours of full rollout
